title: Monte Carlo Methods — Learning from Complete Episodes

questions.question: For a two-step trajectory with rewards [-1.0, -1.0] and gamma=0.99, what does returns_from compute for the first state?
questions.explanation: The first return is -1.0 + 0.99 * (-1.0) = -1.99; returns_from works backward and then restores trajectory order.

questions.question: What does the seen set enforce in mc_policy_evaluation?
options: It prevents an episode from reaching TERMINAL twice
It updates each state only on its first visit within that episode
It forces every action to be sampled exactly once
It removes all states whose return is negative
questions.explanation: The code skips a state once it is in seen, so each episode contributes only its first occurrence to the state-value estimate.

questions.question: What does mc_policy_evaluation return for the uniform policy?
options: Only the last trajectory and its actions
A neural network and a replay buffer
A defaultdict of values and a defaultdict of first-visit counts
A deterministic policy with no value estimates
questions.explanation: The function accumulates V and counts, then returns both so the estimates can be inspected alongside their visit support.

questions.question: How does mc_control choose an action during training when epsilon=0.1?
options: It always takes the action with the largest Q value
It samples from the uniform_policy and ignores Q
It selects a random state instead of an action
It explores randomly with probability 0.1 and otherwise takes the current Q-greedy action
questions.explanation: The nested policy checks local_rng.random() < epsilon, choosing randomly in that case and max(Q[state]) otherwise.

questions.question: When does rollout stop before max_steps=200?
options: Immediately after step reaches TERMINAL and returns done=True
Whenever the reward is -1.0, even if the state is not terminal
After the first repeated state, regardless of the transition
Only when the random generator runs out of values
questions.explanation: rollout appends the transition, updates state, and breaks when done; max_steps is only a safety bound for nonterminating behavior.

questions.question: Why does main print -39.41 as a DP reference for V(0,0)?
options: It is the undiscounted optimal path length
It is the approximate discounted value of the uniform policy in this 4x4 GridWorld
It is the number of episodes used for MC control
It is the terminal reward multiplied by gamma
questions.explanation: The reference comes from evaluating the same uniform-random policy with gamma=0.99; MC estimates should approach it as episodes grow.
